bull_bear.body:
- Only global player with captive PET resin production at every BOPET film manufacturing location, supporting cost competitiveness and supply security
- Second-largest global capacity (ex-China) in thin BOPET films, with ~9% global market share ex-China
- Globally integrated manufacturing footprint across 8 facilities in 5 countries (India, Thailand, Indonesia, Turkey, USA), enabling a balanced on-shoring/near-shoring/off-shoring model
- Deep, long-standing customer relationships (15+ years with most key customers); top 10 film customers contribute only ~26% of turnover, limiting concentration risk
- D-PAC (Differentiated Products, Applications & Customers) strategy driving mix shift to specialty/value-added products, reducing exposure to standard-film pricing cycles
- Leadership in recycled PET films (Sarafil® rPET, up to 100% post-consumer recycled content) via in-house chemical and mechanical recycling in Thailand
- Extensive R&D and downstream integration (metallizing, coating, holography) supporting product differentiation and customer intimacy
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Interest rate risk on floating-rate debt — The Company evaluates shifting some floating-rate debt to fixed rate based on cost-benefit analysis; management notes the impact of significant interest rate movements is minimal as the Company is net cash positive.
- Credit risk from a globally dispersed customer base — Customers span ~85 countries with unsecured/open payment terms, and risk is accentuated by geopolitical uncertainties and economic disruption in certain regions; mitigated by an internal credit management system and global credit insurance cover, though the average credit period rose to 58 days in FY25-26 from 54 days in FY24-25.
- Project implementation risk on new capex — Delay in implementation, cost overrun, inability to stabilize production from new investments, or failure to meet target investment objectives could significantly affect future profitability; flagged specifically for the new BOPET film line in India and smaller specialty-portfolio projects in India and Turkey.
- Geopolitical risk across operating regions — Ongoing conflicts (including the Middle East), trade tensions and political instability can disrupt supply chains, impact demand, and increase volatility in raw material, energy and logistics costs and currency, despite the Company's diversified manufacturing footprint providing some resilience.
- Global supply chain disruption — Reliance on international shipping and logistics exposes the Company to disruption via critical routes such as the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz, which can raise freight costs, extend transit times and affect container availability.
- Regulatory risk in food-contact packaging — Extensive food-safety regulation by bodies such as the USFDA and the EC governs packaging materials across jurisdictions; non-compliance risk is managed through internal processes and continuous monitoring of regulatory developments.
- Health, safety and security risk at manufacturing sites — Exposure to fire incidents, workplace accidents, equipment failures and unauthorized facility access could lead to injury or loss of life, asset damage, operational disruption, financial loss and reputational harm; mitigated via a Health & Safety framework covering fire/emergency management and workplace safety systems.

business.body: Polyplex manufactures a diversified portfolio of polymeric films - BOPET (thin and thick), BOPP, CPP and Blown PP/PE - along with captive PET resin, serving global customers across packaging, electrical & electronics, industrial and specialty applications. Its backward-integrated model (captive PET resin at every film-manufacturing location) is combined with forward/downstream capabilities such as metallizing, coating and holography, and its D-PAC (Differentiated Products, Applications and Customers) strategy is a key pillar of growth into high-value specialty markets.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- **Base Films:** BOPET (thin), BOPET (thick), BOPP, CPP, Blown PP/PE
- **PET Resin:** PET Resin (including mechanically recycled resin)
- **Value-Added / Downstream Films:** Metallizing, Silicone Coating, Extrusion Coating, Transfer Metallized Paper (TMP), Direct Metallized Paper (DMP), Holography, Offline Chemical Coating
- **Specialty / Branded:** Sarafil® rPET films

outlook.body:
- Immediate priority to accelerate the ramp-up of the new U.S. production line while maintaining an optimum and profitable product mix
- Continue to evaluate investment opportunities across both base films and downstream speciality films, with a disciplined approach to capital allocation
- Strengthen market position through operational excellence and a differentiated product portfolio, leveraging diversified manufacturing footprint, integrated operations and strong procurement capabilities to navigate geopolitical disruption and supply chain volatility
- Deepen the D-PAC (Differentiated Products, Applications and Customers) strategic focus, expanding into emerging high-value applications (release liners, labels, lithium-ion batteries, digital printing) to enhance value realization and reduce exposure to cyclical pricing pressures
- Deepen backward integration into PET resin and downstream integration (metallizing, coating, silicone coating, holography, transfer metallized products, recycling) to strengthen quality, supply reliability, cost competitiveness and operational flexibility
- Advance circular economy leadership through the Thailand recycling platform (chemical and mechanical recycling), Sarafil® rPET films with up to 100% PCR content, and development of mono-material, PVC-free and paper-replacement sustainable solutions
- Expand renewable energy adoption and sustainable solutions across solar photovoltaics, lithium-ion batteries, transfer metallized films and recyclable PET structures
- Operate under the guiding theme 'Innovating today, shaping tomorrow', leveraging diversified manufacturing platform, specialized product portfolio and strong customer relationships to navigate a dynamic environment and capitalize on emerging opportunities
- The Board recommended a Final Dividend of INR 1 per equity share (face value INR 10) for FY2025-26, for shareholders' approval by ordinary resolution at the 41st AGM on September 8, 2026. The Company has no Joint Ventures as at 31.03.2026. Governance-related capital/board practices adopted on a discretionary basis (Para E, Schedule II of the Listing Regulations) include maintaining a Non-Executive Chairperson's office, moving towards a regime of financial statements with unmodified audit opinions, and having the Internal Auditor report directly (reflecting a broader discipline around financial reporting quality rather than a stated capital-allocation philosophy).
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Polyplex's committed growth capex pipeline (~USD 73 million) comprises three projects: a new BOPET film line in India (Bazpur) with a capital cost of USD 56 Mn, expected commissioning Q4 FY26-27, adding upcoming capacity of ~52,400 MT of BOPET thin film; two new metallizers in India with a capital cost of USD 7 Mn, expected commissioning Q4 FY26-27, adding ~17,000 MT of metallizing capacity; and an additional offline coater in Turkey with a capital cost of USD 10 Mn, expected commissioning Q2 FY26-27, adding ~158 Mn sqm of coated-film capacity. These investments are aimed at optimizing India's cost structure while strengthening the specialty portfolio and deepening downstream integration. This growth pipeline follows FY25-26 milestones of commissioning a new PET film line and an offline coater (OLC) in the United States, augmenting TMP capacity in India, and the acquisition of a 51% stake in TechNova Printrite Products Private Limited (since renamed Polyplex DigiPrint Private Limited, PDPL), which added digital print media, coating technology and application-engineering capabilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Following the U.S. Supreme Court decision rendering reciprocal tariffs invalid, early signs of recovery are emerging in the U.S., improving the near-term outlook
- Evolving tariff dynamics and changes in U.S. trade policy have strengthened customer preference for locally sourced products, enhancing the outlook for the U.S. facility
- Additional BOPET capacity is expected to come onstream in China over the next one to three years, but management remains confident in the industry's long-term growth prospects
- Global thin BOPET film growth is expected at about 5% for the next few years, with demand in India expected to continue growing at ~10%, driven by FMCG expansion
- Industry-wide oversupply is expected to continue in the short-to-medium term, but capacity utilization (CUF) is expected to improve gradually with a pause in ex-China capacity additions, closure of older inefficient lines and rising demand
- Thick BOPET film demand is expected to show a steady CAGR of ~4-5%, supported by Electrical & Electronics applications (MLCC films, OLED displays, AI-related applications, autonomous vehicle electronics) which command premium pricing, while photovoltaic film demand has slowed as solar manufacturers shift to glass panels
- Global BOPP demand is expected to grow at more than 4%, driven by recession-proof food packaging and e-commerce-driven demand for labels and tape base film; in India, several new BOPP lines were commissioned in FY25-26 with an additional 8-10 lines expected over the next 1-2 years, likely pressuring industry margins, partially offset by a competitor's capacity shutdown following a fire incident in May 2025
- The easing of reciprocal tariffs, partially offset by Section 301 tariffs, is expected to support a gradual recovery in margins in the U.S.
- The ongoing conflict in the Middle East continues to create uncertainty affecting raw material prices, energy markets and global supply chains
